rubrics.rubric: Does February_2026_Referral_Audit.xlsx provide a complete, source-grounded Referral Log with accurate code and referral-status auditing?
criterion: The workbook contains the tabs Referral Log, Discrepancy Report, and Summary Dashboard in that order.
Referral Log contains every input referral and every original input column plus ICD-10 Valid (Y/N), Code Discrepancy Notes, Duplicate Flag, and Status.
Status uses only New, Under Review, Pending Records, Scheduled, Completed, or Cancelled and reflects the available referral, appointment, record, imaging, and authorization evidence.
Each ICD-10 code is checked against the supplied code list for M00-M99 chapter membership and official description match.

Chapter membership and clinical narrative or laterality match are reported separately, so a valid injury or pain code outside M00-M99 is not mislabeled as clinically invalid merely because it is outside the tracked chapter.
Laterality or narrative mismatches are identified, and a corrected code is supplied only when the narrative makes it determinable.
Duplicate flags identify the matching Referral_ID rather than using an unexplained generic marker.

rubrics.rubric: Does Discrepancy Report include every material data-quality issue with the relevant evidence and an actionable, row-specific correction path?
criterion: The sheet uses the required fields Referral ID, Patient Name, Issue Type, Relevant Fields, and Recommended Corrective Action.
It includes code validity, description or laterality mismatch, missing records or imaging, authorization, duplicate-referral, and other material identifier anomalies supported by the input.
Shared identifiers across different patient identities are treated as a data-quality issue distinct from duplicate rows for the same patient.
Relevant Fields states the conflicting or missing values needed to understand each issue.
For a determinable laterality mismatch, the action states the corrected code and identifies the clinical risk of acting on the wrong side.
Every corrective action names the affected row's contact person, practice, fax number, and fax or other instructed contact method.
Duplicate-referral actions name the matching Referral_ID and recommend consolidation.

rubrics.rubric: Does Summary Dashboard provide accurate, reconcilable counts for the categories requested by the instructions?
criterion: The dashboard reports counts by referring physician.
The dashboard reports counts by insurance provider.
The dashboard reports counts by urgency level.
The dashboard reports missing-record and missing-imaging counts separately.
The dashboard reports authorization-status issues and total discrepancies.
Dashboard totals reconcile to Referral Log and Discrepancy Report.

rubrics.rubric: Does Referral Log apply the required conditional formatting without losing either signal when conditions overlap?
criterion: Every row whose Urgency is Urgent receives visible red formatting.
Every Records_Received = No cell or row receives visible yellow formatting.
Every Imaging_Received = No cell or row receives visible yellow formatting.
A referral that is both urgent and missing records or imaging visibly retains both signals, such as red row formatting plus yellow missing-item cells.
The rules are based on cell values or equivalent complete row coverage rather than manually formatting only selected examples.

rubrics.rubric: Does Records_and_Clarification_Request.docx function as the requested dual-purpose, privacy-aware fax template?
criterion: The document has distinct Missing Documentation Request and Coding Discrepancy Clarification sections.
It contains merge fields for patient, referring physician, discrepancy details, and the missing-document list.
The coding section clearly asks the referring office to confirm a code-versus-narrative discrepancy.
It references an attached HIPAA authorization release form and 45 CFR 164.508 without claiming that authorization is unnecessary.
It includes a confidentiality notice and a 10-business-day response deadline.
It uses the supplied Heartland practice identity and contact information.

rubrics.rubric: Does Referral_Acknowledgment_Letter.docx contain the complete validated-referral acknowledgment requested by the practice?
criterion: The template includes the required patient, referring-physician, appointment-date, ICD-10-code, and diagnosis merge fields.
It states the appointment date and assigned physician.
It confirms that the diagnosis code and diagnosis were verified.
It states that a consultation report will follow the appointment.
It references the practice's Notice of Privacy Practices and uses the supplied practice identity and contact information.

rubrics.rubric: Does February_2026_Action_Plan.docx assign every needed follow-up to the correct priority tier with complete execution details?
criterion: The document contains Tier 1, Tier 2, and Tier 3 sections using the instructed 24-48 hour, 5-business-day, and administrative definitions.
Every referral needing follow-up is covered; distinct follow-up needs for one referral may be listed separately, while a combined item uses a clearly justified applicable tier.
Urgent unresolved clinical issues, including time-sensitive coordination stated in Referral_Reason or Notes, are placed in Tier 1.
Routine documentation or authorization gaps are placed in Tier 2 unless a source-supported clinical issue requires Tier 1; a separate administrative task may be listed in Tier 3.
Routine rescheduling and other non-clinical follow-up are placed in Tier 3 when represented as distinct administrative tasks.
Each item names the patient, Referral_ID, required action, correspondence template, recipient name, practice, fax number, and deadline.
Tier assignments and actions are consistent with the Referral Log, Discrepancy Report, and free-text referral notes.

rubrics.rubric: Are the external references and formatting sources used accurately without adding unsupported legal or clinical conclusions?
criterion: ICD-10 descriptions and laterality are consistent with the supplied k4m1113 M00-M99 code file for codes within that range.
Codes outside M00-M99 are marked as outside the tracked range and assessed against the narrative without being treated as nonexistent; naming their actual chapter is optional supporting detail.
HIPAA authorization language is consistent with the supplied Pacific Orthopaedic Associates reference form and 45 CFR 164.508.
Both correspondence templates use Heartland Orthopedic Specialists letterhead content laid out in a manner reasonably guided by the CRMC referral form; no exact visual imitation is required.
